result.title: Dense Flow from Adaptive Correspondence
result.summary: Optical flow requires reliable matching from sufficient visual context and precise motion at every pixel. Existing methods such as WAFT match and estimate flow on the same coarse grids, then recover dense flow through learned upsampling, without explicitly linking visual support for matching to dense flow reconstruction. Our key insight is that dense pixel-level flow does not require equally dense matching. We decouple correspondence scale from flow resolution by adapting the size and shape of spatial supports to image structure for reliable matching, while reusing these supports for precise dense flow reconstruction. We realize this in Flow from Adaptive Token Estimation (FATE), whose token supports expand within coherent regions and contract near motion boundaries. Shared pixel-to-token associations pool features for matching and reconstruct pixel flow from token motions. Flow supervision jointly trains pixel grouping, token matching, and flow estimation without grouping labels, allowing FATE to anticipate which pixels are likely to move together from appearance alone. Trained on FlyingChairs/FlyingThings3D, FATE achieves the highest zero-shot accuracy on Sintel Final and KITTI, a critical setting given scarce real-world flow labels. For visible pixels, FATE improves accuracy within coherent regions, and more near motion boundaries. Its largest gains occur where direct matches are unavailable: Occluded or out-of-frame pixels account for roughly 10% of valid pixels but 50% of WAFT's total error. Experiments show that adaptive correspondence through pixel-to-token grouping enables reliable matching and precise pixel-level flow, improving generalization to unseen real scenes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 FATE，把对应关系的尺度与光流分辨率解耦：token 支持区域在纹理一致区内扩张、在运动边界处收缩，用共享的像素—token 关联同时完成匹配与稠密流重建，并以流监督在无分组标签下联合训练分组、匹配与估计。
AI.relevance_reason: 其由任务监督学出的像素分组与自适应支持区域，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选和动态 token 粒度提供启发，但该工作属低层运动估计，与多模态推理状态的关联仍需核查。
